headline: Tabbed Settings and a custom-name click
notes: **Settings is now three short tabs: Naming, Bins and Panel.** One page each instead of one long sheet. Rest the pointer on anything and the line above Save says what it does

**Naming shows what each click makes.** One row each for Click, ⌘-click (Ctrl-click on Windows) and Alt-click on Project, with the exact name it would give. Every row starts closed, so the tab stays short; open one with its arrow to change it. Client, project, initials and the date now have their own labelled section

**A warning when you open an old project file.** Open Job_v02 while Job_v04 sits beside it and the amber banner names the newer file, with a **Show folder** button. With *Block VersionUp on an old version* on (Settings → Panel), Project will not save from the old file

**Hold ⌘ (Ctrl on Windows) and click Version up to use your Custom name.** Your everyday format stays on a plain click; ⌘-click makes that one version with your own pattern, which now always shows in Settings → Naming. It needs {version}, and {name} is now one of the tokens you can tap in. Rest on the button and the ⌘ row shows the exact name. The old-version warning still recognises the cut

**Hold Shift for a new major version, whatever your naming format.** Brand Film_v03 becomes Brand Film_v04.1, keeping the name's own shape, custom patterns included. Rest on Version up and the Shift row shows the exact name

**Alt-click now files the alternative and opens it.** It goes into its own ALT bin, or stays beside the original if you prefer (Settings → Bins), and it is put in your timeline, because that is where you wanted to be. The original is never touched
**Click a sequence in the version list to open it.** The row you are on is marked
**The hover read-out uses your real sequence.** With one sequence selected, each row shows exactly the name that press would make
**No more frozen animation while it works.** Press a button and it quietly steps back to grey while Premiere takes over, then eases into the result instead of jumping
**Green means done, on every button.** A clean run now turns green whichever button you pressed, alongside amber for partly done and red for failed
**The hover read-out fits a short panel.** Docked short, it becomes one line that changes as you hold ⌘, Alt or Shift, with small key marks to show there is more
**New bins go beside your sequences,** not at the top of the project. This changes a fresh install only; settings you have already saved are left alone

**The ☰ menu is four items, so it fits a short dock:** Tour, Help & licence…, Send feedback…, then Settings… at the bottom. Help, your licence and the update check are now one window. It checks for updates by itself when you open it, and **Check for updates**, at the bottom, tells you straight away whether you're on the latest version. Hover tips also appear a little sooner

**Your licence is kept safer.** It now lives in its own file with a backup, so a Premiere upgrade or an interrupted save cannot lose it, and a key pasted from an email with odd dashes or spaces is still read correctly
Fixed: a year in a title, like Showreel 2026_v11, was read as part of the version, and a date like Promo_2026-09-27 could be read as a version number
Fixed: versioning a whole bin could also renumber the old copies already filed inside it, and approving twice put an APPROVED bin inside APPROVED
Fixed: "Same folder, no bin" for an alternative put it at the top of the project
Fixed: Project could save over an existing file when a folder name contained # or %. It now refuses rather than risk it
Fixed: a client, project or initials containing characters like / : ? made a file name Windows cannot save
Fixed: the panel could stay on "Loading…" if Premiere started with it docked very short, and could overlap itself in a short, wide dock
Fixed: pressing a second button while one was still working could start two jobs at once
Fixed: Settings closed and said "saved" when a bin name was left empty. It now stays open on the right tab and says which box needs filling
Fixed: Shift could raise a year that sat in front of the version, so NK Showreel 2026.1 became 2027.1. The year is now left alone
Fixed: a ⌘-click (Ctrl-click on Windows) on a dotted name like Edit_v0.3 now gives v0.4, and a 001-style series keeps counting 002, 003 rather than restarting at v01
Fixed: choosing a saved preset in Settings replaced your ⌘ pattern, and Save could rewrite the preset. Presets now change only when you press Save preset
Fixed: opening Help & licence brought back an update banner you had dismissed with Not now
Fixed: your client and project names went missing after Project made the next project file
Fixed: after your first ⌘ version up, opening the old cut gave no warning that it was old
Fixed: the ☰ menu could run off the bottom of a short docked panel. It now scrolls
